featured.title: Nepal Flood Death Toll Surges Past 330 as Glacier Collapse Scale Becomes Clear
featured.excerpt: Scientists confirm an ice-rock avalanche, not an earthquake, triggered one of Nepal's worst natural disasters, with over 900 people still missing including dozens of Americans and 177 Indian pilgrims.
featured.image_caption: An aerial view shows houses buried under mud and debris following flash floods in Nepal on August 26, 2026. The floods killed over 330 people and left more than 900 missing across eight districts.
featured.nri_angle: 177 Indian pilgrims en route to Kailash Mansarovar are among the missing, 63 Americans unaccounted for, and downstream flooding prompted evacuations in Bihar — the disaster has direct implications for diaspora families across South Asia.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

editorial.title: Who Is Anima Anandkumar? The Mysore-Born Scientist Who Turned Down a Bezos-Backed Fortune — and Is Building AI That Understands Physics, Not Words
editorial.image_caption: Anima Anandkumar speaking at the AAAS Annual Meeting in 2026. The Caltech professor was named a TIME100 AI Innovator days after launching her physics-focused AI startup, Accelerated Understanding.

just_in.title: Publicis Wins PepsiCo's $5.4 Billion Media Account, Exits Coca-Cola Pitch
just_in.excerpt: The French agency group displaces Omnicom as PepsiCo's lead global media partner in a deal covering 200-plus markets, and withdraws from rival Coca-Cola's ongoing review.
just_in.image_caption: PepsiCo's global headquarters in Purchase, New York. The company awarded its 5.4 billion dollar media account to Publicis Groupe, which exited the competing Coca-Cola pitch to secure the deal.
just_in.nri_angle: Publicis already handled PepsiCo's media in India and several Asian markets; the global consolidation puts Indian advertising professionals at the center of a unified 200-market operation.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: SpiceJet to Add 20 Aircraft and Target 200 Daily Flights Ahead of Winter Travel Rush
just_in.excerpt: The budget carrier has finalised lease agreements for 15 Boeing and five Airbus planes, with deliveries starting mid-October ahead of the Durga Puja travel surge.
just_in.image_caption: A SpiceJet aircraft on the tarmac at an Indian airport. The airline plans to add 20 leased planes to its fleet ahead of the winter travel season.
just_in.nri_angle: NRIs planning winter trips to India may see more route options and competitive fares as SpiceJet ramps capacity on high-demand domestic corridors during the festive travel season.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: India Returns to 'A' Category After 35 Years as Japan's JCR Upgrades Sovereign Rating
just_in.excerpt: The Japan Credit Rating Agency raised India's long-term issuer rating from BBB+ to A-, citing 7.7% GDP growth, banking sector health, and structural reforms.
just_in.image_caption: A credit rating dial showing investment-grade tiers. Japan Credit Rating Agency upgraded India to A- from BBB+, the highest sovereign rating India holds from any agency.
just_in.nri_angle: The A- rating from Japan's JCR may boost confidence among Japanese and global institutional investors in India, potentially benefiting NRI portfolios and India-focused funds.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: BSE Gains as CEO Says NSE Cannot List on Own Platform, Setting Up India's Biggest IPO Battle
just_in.excerpt: BSE CEO Sundararaman Ramamurthy's declaration that NSE must list on a rival exchange positions BSE as the sole venue for what could be India's largest-ever IPO.
just_in.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai. BSE shares surged after NSE's CEO confirmed the rival exchange cannot list on its own platform, setting up a battle over India's biggest IPO.
just_in.nri_angle: NRI investors tracking the NSE IPO — expected to be one of India's largest — should note that trading will initially be on BSE, with regulatory uncertainty around whether NSE shares can eventually trade on NSE's own platform.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Tata Trusts Cleared in 1989 Share Transfer Probe, Removing Hurdle to Tata Sons Chairman Search
just_in.excerpt: Maharashtra's Charity Commissioner closed a complaint over the transfer of 833 Tata Sons shares, a ruling that frees the Trusts to resume internal governance at a critical leadership juncture.

just_in.title: Sensex Put Options Spike 500% as Closing Auction Triggers Another 2,100-Point Swing
just_in.excerpt: India's new closing auction session caused the Sensex to briefly plunge 2,100 points on expiry day, sending put option premiums surging and reigniting calls for SEBI to intervene.
just_in.image_caption: A SEBI office building in Mumbai. The regulator introduced the closing auction session on August 3 to determine official closing prices for F&O-eligible stocks.

just_in.title: Belgian PM's Chocolate India Gate Melts En Route as India and Belgium Reset Ties After 20 Years

just_in.nri_angle: The India-Belgium diplomatic reset and India-EU FTA talks could expand business and educational opportunities for the Indian diaspora in Europe.

just_in.title: Your Organs Age on Their Own Schedules — And a New Study Shows They're in Sync
just_in.excerpt: Scientists analyzed 25,000 organ images and found the human body ages in distinct waves, with the ovaries acting as a potential pacemaker for whole-body aging.
just_in.image_caption: Scientists found that individual organs age at different rates but are more synchronized than previously thought. The study maps biological age across multiple organ systems.
just_in.nri_angle: The research has broad health implications for aging populations worldwide, including South Asian communities with higher cardiovascular and metabolic disease risk factors.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Gold Jumps 2% as Fed's Waller Cools Rate Hike Expectations
just_in.excerpt: Spot gold surged past $4,470 an ounce after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller signaled openness to holding rates steady, pulling the dollar to a one-week low.
just_in.nri_angle: Gold price swings affect NRI investment portfolios and remittance calculations tied to dollar-rupee exchange rates.

just_in.title: Preity Zinta Worked 18-Hour Days on Vibe to Get Back to Her Kids in the US
just_in.excerpt: The actor addressed Bollywood's work-hours debate at the trailer launch of her upcoming spy comedy, saying her grueling schedule was a personal choice driven by motherhood.
just_in.image_caption: Preity Zinta, the Bollywood actress, spoke about her grueling schedule on the set of Vibe and the pull of returning to her children in the United States.
just_in.nri_angle: Zinta's perspective as an NRI mother balancing Hollywood-adjacent life in LA with Bollywood commitments resonates with diaspora families navigating dual-country careers.

just_in.title: Qualcomm Unveils AI-Powered Adreno Neural Fusion GPU for Next Snapdragon Flagship
just_in.excerpt: The chipmaker's next-gen mobile processor will embed dedicated AI matrix cores directly in the GPU pipeline, promising 40% power savings and a major leap in mobile gaming graphics.
just_in.image_caption: Qualcomm unveiled its next-generation Snapdragon chipset with an AI-powered Adreno Neural Fusion GPU designed for on-device inference.
just_in.nri_angle: Qualcomm employs thousands of engineers in India, particularly at its Hyderabad and Bengaluru R&D centres, and the new chip will power flagship Android devices popular among the diaspora.

just_in.title: Delhi Court Grants Bail to AAP's Satyendar Jain in Jal Board Corruption Case
just_in.excerpt: The former Delhi water minister was ordered to furnish a personal bond of Rs 2 lakh after spending over two weeks in judicial custody on charges of manipulating sewage treatment plant tenders.
just_in.image_caption: Satyendar Jain, the AAP leader, was granted bail by a Delhi court in a Jal Board corruption case.
just_in.nri_angle: The case adds to the string of legal battles facing AAP leaders, a party that drew significant NRI support during its anti-corruption campaigns.

just_in.title: Canada Probes Import Risks After India Raid Uncovers Fake Labels on Food Products
just_in.excerpt: The Canadian Food Inspection Agency is the first foreign regulator to respond after Indian authorities seized nearly $80,000 worth of relabelled PepsiCo, Nestle and Coca-Cola products from a Mumbai warehouse.
just_in.image_caption: Food safety authorities inspect product labels at a facility. Canadian regulators are investigating import risks after Indian agencies uncovered fake labels on food products meant for export.
just_in.nri_angle: The incident raises safety concerns for Indian diaspora communities in Canada who regularly purchase imported Indian food products.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Telangana CM Sacks Minister Konda Surekha From Cabinet Over Party Indiscipline
just_in.excerpt: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy removed the Forest and Environment minister after Congress high command backed disciplinary action triggered by her daughter's public attacks on party leadership.
just_in.image_caption: Konda Surekha was sacked from the Telangana cabinet by Chief Minister Revanth Reddy over party indiscipline.
just_in.nri_angle: The internal Congress turmoil in Telangana is closely watched by NRIs from the state who maintain strong ties to regional politics.

news.excerpt: India's April-June growth comfortably beat forecasts, driven by an investment surge and manufacturing strength, but critics question whether a base-year revision inflated the headline figure.

news.nri_angle: India's GDP credibility debate affects NRI equity investments, rupee-denominated assets, and global capital allocation to Indian markets.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Google Escapes Ad Tech Breakup as Judge Rejects DOJ Forced Sale
news.excerpt: Federal judge opts for behavioral remedies over structural separation, marking the third consecutive failure by U.S. antitrust enforcers to break up a major tech company.
news.image_caption: The Googleplex, Google's corporate headquarters in Mountain View, California. A federal judge rejected the DOJ's demand that Google sell off its ad technology business.
news.nri_angle: The ruling affects the broader tech industry where many Indian-origin professionals work, and has implications for digital advertising costs that impact Indian-American small business owners.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Modi Demands End to Terror Double Standards at SCO Summit in Bishkek
news.excerpt: At the 26th SCO Summit in Kyrgyzstan, PM Modi called for dismantling the entire ecosystem of terrorism while sharing warm exchanges with Xi Jinping and Putin — as Pakistan's Sharif stood by without interaction.
news.image_caption: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the SCO Summit. Modi called on member states to end double standards on terrorism and pushed for greater counter-terror cooperation.
news.nri_angle: India's anti-terrorism stance and frozen India-Pakistan ties directly affect diaspora communities through visa policies, security postures, and bilateral relations.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Both Parents' Vitamin B12 Levels Linked to Birth Defect Risk, Major Study Finds
news.excerpt: A large prospective study from China shows that higher B12 in fathers — not just mothers — before conception is associated with fewer birth defects, a finding with outsized implications for India's B12-deficient population.
news.image_caption: An expectant couple during pregnancy. A large prospective study found that higher vitamin B12 levels in both parents before conception are linked to a lower risk of birth defects.
news.nri_angle: Vitamin B12 deficiency affects an estimated 40–75% of India's population, making these findings directly relevant to Indian families planning pregnancies — especially those on vegetarian diets.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Centre Defers Manipur Census Amid Protests Over NRC and Ethnic Tensions
news.excerpt: The September 1 house-listing exercise was put on hold after Amit Shah chaired a review and civil-society groups demanded an NRC update first.
news.nri_angle: Diaspora members from Manipur face continued uncertainty as institutional governance stalls in the state.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Three Killed in Armed Attack on Manipur Village as Naga-Kuki Violence Escalates
news.excerpt: Suspected militants opened fire on a Kuki-inhabited village in Kangpokpi, killing three and critically injuring four.
news.nri_angle: Ongoing ethnic violence in Manipur remains a concern for diaspora families with roots in the northeastern state.

news.title: India Records Warmest August Since 1901 as Monsoon Deficit Hits 14%
news.excerpt: El Niño-driven heat and feeble rainfall leave nearly half of India’s districts parched, with September offering little relief for crops and reservoirs.
news.image_caption: India recorded its warmest August since 1901, with temperatures 0.67°C above the long-period average as monsoon rainfall lagged 14% below normal.
news.nri_angle: India’s monsoon deficit threatens crop yields and food prices, which directly impacts diaspora families’ relatives in agricultural states and could drive up import costs for Indian staples abroad.

carousel.excerpt: India's cricket board convened captains Shubman Gill and Shreyas Iyer alongside head coach Gautam Gambhir at its Mumbai headquarters to dissect recent series losses and chart a roadmap to the 2027 ODI World Cup.
carousel.image_caption: Rohit Sharma, the Indian cricket captain, faces questions about his ODI future following a high-level BCCI review.
carousel.nri_angle: Indian cricket's direction ahead of the 2027 World Cup is closely watched by millions of diaspora fans who follow every tour and selection decision.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: Harvard Engineers Bacteria to Pull CO2 From Air Into Seawater 2.6 Times Faster
carousel.excerpt: A genetically modified marine bacterium accelerates rock weathering by stripping rust from mineral surfaces, offering a new biological pathway for industrial-scale carbon removal.
carousel.image_caption: Engineered bacteria designed for carbon capture. Harvard researchers modified E. coli bacteria to pull carbon dioxide from air into seawater at 2.6 times the natural rate.
carousel.nri_angle: The research involves Indian-origin scientist Amogh Jalihal as co-author, and the carbon removal technology has implications for India's climate commitments and coastal infrastructure.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: India Returns to 'A' Category After 35 Years as Japan's JCR Upgrades Sovereign Rating
carousel.excerpt: The Japan Credit Rating Agency raised India's long-term issuer rating from BBB+ to A-, citing 7.7% GDP growth, banking sector health, and structural reforms.
carousel.image_caption: A credit rating dial showing investment-grade tiers. Japan Credit Rating Agency upgraded India to A- from BBB+, the highest sovereign rating India holds from any agency.
carousel.nri_angle: The A- rating from Japan's JCR may boost confidence among Japanese and global institutional investors in India, potentially benefiting NRI portfolios and India-focused funds.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk
